title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 3rd draft, June 1986). F is a set of 'figures' carrying a partial order <= (inclusion), a relation << (roughly 'relatively compact in' or 'contained in the interior of'), and a symmetric disjointness relation || (also written //). For a part A of F, the complement is ∁A = {G : G || F for all F in A}. This is the polarity (Galois connection) of a symmetric relation. Σ^0_F is the set of 'supports', the parts with A = ∁∁A.

Previous page, items (vii)-(x):
- Σ^0_F is a complete lattice. Inf is intersection; sup is the double complement of the union.
- ∁ is an order-reversing involution.
- A ∩ ∁A = {∅_F}, because the empty figure is the only self-disjoint figure.
- So (Σ^0_F, ∁) is a complete ortholattice.
- The bottom element is {∅_F}, not the empty part, since ∅_F is disjoint from everything.

This page:
1. It first ends a remark that finite sups need not behave like set-theoretic unions.
2. It then flags the real issue: it is not clear in general that P ∧ ⋁_i Q_i = ⋁_i (P ∧ Q_i) holds in Σ^0_F, even for finite joins. This is distributivity of the 'intersection of supports' over their 'sums'. If it held, Σ^0_F would be a complete Boolean algebra, since a distributive ortholattice is Boolean.
3. Grothendieck says this 'tends to be true' for the structure map of (*) in the situations he has in mind, with a forward reference.
4. He then says the same development can be redone for a structure (M, <=, <<, ∦), where M is presumably a set of smaller or 'point-like' figures, using only the relation ||_M. This gives Σ^0_M, the bicommutant-closed parts of M ('M-supports').
5. There is a canonical bijection Σ^0_M ⇄ Σ^0_F. It is an isomorphism of ordered sets, built from the bijections of p.61, and it commutes with the complement operation.
6. In Σ^0_M the bottom is the genuinely empty part and the top is M, because M contains no empty figure.

Marginal note: for A closed under <=, Cos-W_F(A) ∩ L = Cos-W_F(A ∩ L), and Cos-W_F(F) ∩ L = Cos-W_L(F). This prepares the next page. There, M is generalised to any Λ ⊂ F satisfying the density condition Disj_Λ: F // G iff every X in the 'shadow' omb_Λ(F) = {X in Λ : X << F} is // G. One then gets cosmpr_F(A) = cosmpr_F(omb_Λ A), and for A closed under << the shadow is just A ∩ Λ.

Purpose: build a point-free, figure-based 'tame topology'. The algebra of 'regular' supports should be intrinsic, so that it can be computed equally from all figures or from any 'dense' family of small figures.
errors: No error. The doubt about distributivity is justified: the closed sets of an arbitrary orthogonality relation form an ortholattice that need not be distributive (e.g. orthogonality of vectors gives the subspace lattice). Distributivity does hold, giving a complete Boolean algebra, whenever || coincides with 'having no nonempty common subfigure' for <=. Grothendieck does not state this sufficient condition here.
The order isomorphism Σ^0_M ≅ Σ^0_F is asserted with a pointer to p.61 but not proved on this page. On the next page it rests on the density hypothesis Disj_Λ, which is exactly what is needed.

ideas.what: Supports as bicommutant-closed parts for a symmetric disjointness relation, forming a complete ortholattice with ∁ as orthocomplement
ideas.modern_name: Polarity / Galois connection of an orthogonality space; complete ortholattice of closed subsets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (Lattice Theory, 1940); orthogonality spaces: Dacey 1968, Foulis–Randall

ideas.what: The question of whether Σ^0 is distributive, i.e. Boolean
ideas.modern_name: Distributivity of an ortholattice (Boolean vs orthomodular / 'quantum logic'); regular open algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff–von Neumann 1936; regular open algebras: Tarski, Stone

ideas.what: Canonical order isomorphism between closed sets computed on a dense subfamily M (or Λ) of figures and on all figures, commuting with complement
ideas.modern_name: Dense-subset invariance of the regular-open (Boolean) completion; separative quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Forcing literature (Cohen, Scott, Solovay, 1960s); Boolean completions of posets

ideas.what: Axiomatising topology by figures with part-of <=, 'well-inside' <<, and disjointness rather than by points
ideas.modern_name: Mereotopology / point-free geometry (non-tangential proper part, connection relation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead 1929, de Laguna 1922, Tarski 1929, Clarke 1981, Randell–Cui–Cohn (RCC) 1992; proximity spaces (Efremovich)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) calls for a 'tame topology' but does not give this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 analysis-situs axiomatics independently rediscovers the framework of mereotopology / region-based point-free topology. Its ingredients are figures, part-of, a 'well-inside' relation <<, disjointness, regular 'supports' forming an orthocomplemented lattice, and reconstruction from a dense set of small regions. These correspond to Whitehead–Tarski–Clarke and later to RCC and contact algebras (Düntsch–Vakarelov), whose canonical models are regular-closed/regular-open Boolean algebras. Literature on his tame-topology programme seems not to link it to this tradition.
missed.quote: Toute cette suite se répéterait dans le cadre des structures (M, ≤, ≪, ∦)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Results from contact algebras and mereotopology (representation theorems, when the region algebra is Boolean) could answer the open questions in these notes. Conversely, Grothendieck's 'tame' requirements could suggest o-minimal or definable models of mereotopology.

missed.claim: Distributivity of the lattice of supports (Boolean vs merely orthocomplemented) is left as 'tends to be true' with a forward reference. A clean sufficient criterion would settle it: disjointness equals 'no nonempty common lower bound', i.e. the forcing-style incompatibility relation. In that case Σ^0 is the regular-open algebra RO, hence a complete Boolean algebra.
missed.quote: Il n'est pas clair non plus, en général, que l'on ait, dans Σ^0_F, P ∧ ⋁ Q_i = ⋁ (P ∧ Q_i) … Pourtant, cela a tendance à être vrai
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Answering it is minor, but it marks where Grothendieck's figure-theoretic analysis situs touches non-distributive (quantum-logic-like) lattices.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is standard Galois-connection and ortholattice theory. Its interest is historical: it documents Grothendieck building, in 1986, a point-free 'figure' axiomatics for tame topology that parallels mereotopology and Boolean completions without citing them. That framework is largely unknown outside the archive.
